senses.gloss: m. (יָאַשׁ) despairing of recovering a lost object, resignation.
units: <cite ref="Bava Kamma 66a:11">B. Kam. 66ᵃ</cite> <he>י׳ אינו קונה</he> the owner’s resignation gives the robber no right of possession (and he must restore the object itself, not its equivalent).

<cite ref="Bava Kamma 66b:1">Ib.ᵇ</cite> <he>ואי ס״ד י׳ קנה וכ׳</he> and if we should assume that resignation gives a right of possession, how could the robber say, Here is thy property before thee (since in the meantime it has become valueless)?—
<cite ref="Bava Metzia 21b:4">B. Mets. 21ᵇ</cite> top <he>י׳ שלא מדעת</he> unconscious resignation, i.e. a thing which, if missed, is usually given up, but which has as yet not been missed.
<cite ref="Bava Metzia 21b:4">Ib.</cite> <he>הוי י׳</he> is considered as given up.
<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Bava Kamma 4:8:2">Y. B. Kam. IV, end, 4ᶜ</cite> <he>י׳ טעות</he> a resignation under a false presumption; a. fr.
